evidence.quote: The railroad paralleling El Jobean Road was abandoned in 1981. El Jobean Road was widened into the former railroad right of way between Murdock and El Jobean in the 1990s.

evidence.claim: Dearborn, Harvard and Yale carry names borrowed from Chicago streets.
evidence.quote: Some streets, such as Dearborn, Harvard, and Yale, are named after those in Chicago.

evidence.claim: The three brothers who developed Englewood named it for their hometown of Englewood, Chicago; the Florida town’s original plat was filed in August 1896.
evidence.quote: The original plat of Englewood was recorded and filed on August 17, 1896.

evidence.claim: That was a difficult time for local citrus.
evidence.quote: The Great Freeze of 1894 and 1895, along with a bad freeze in 1896, led to the decimation of many local orange plants.

evidence.claim: Freezes in 1894, 1895 and 1896 destroyed many orange plants, and the 1897 Manatee County General Directory listed fish as Englewood’s chief product.
evidence.quote: The Great Freeze of 1894 and 1895, along with a bad freeze in 1896, led to the decimation of many local orange plants. For this reason, by 1897, a Manatee County General Directory listed fish as the chief product for Englewood.

evidence.claim: Dearborn Street also belonged to an early Tamiami Trail alignment, before the highway shifted north and bypassed Englewood by the 1930s.
evidence.quote: Englewood Road (via present-day Old Englewood Road), Dearborn Street, and River Road were part of an early segment of the Tamiami Trail through Englewood. By the 1930s, the Tamiami Trail was rerouted to its current route further north bypassing Englewood.

evidence.claim: The three brothers who developed Englewood named it for their hometown of Englewood, Chicago
evidence.quote: The area was developed by three brothers, and the name Englewood came from their hometown, Englewood, Chicago.

evidence.claim: Beach Road crosses Lemon Bay from Englewood to Manasota Key, with the Gulf of Mexico along the key’s western edge.
evidence.quote: Its western edge is the Gulf of Mexico, and to the east is Lemon Bay, an estuary. The community of Englewood Beach occupies most of the CDP, and it is connected to the mainland by Beach Road, which crosses Lemon Bay to Englewood.

evidence.claim: The 11-mile peninsula became a barrier island through construction of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway.
evidence.quote: "Manasota Key" refers to an 11-mile-long (18 km) peninsula (transformed into a barrier island by the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway)

evidence.claim: Its name came from the Manasota Lumber Company, which operated a Woodmere sawmill from 1918 to 1923.
evidence.quote: The name originated from Manasota Lumber Company, a Maryland-based timber company with a sawmill in Woodmere from 1918 to 1923.

evidence.claim: Manasota combines manatee and Sarasota.
evidence.quote: Manasota is a portmanteau of manatee and Sarasota.

evidence.claim: At the southern end, Stump Pass connects the bay with the Gulf and separates Manasota Key from Don Pedro Island.
evidence.quote: Stump Pass is a channel that connects Lemon Bay to the Gulf of Mexico and separates Manasota Key from Don Pedro Island to the south.

evidence.claim: El Jobean sits off SR 776 on the Myakka River’s northern bank.
evidence.quote: It is located off State Road 776, on the northern banks of the Myakka River.

evidence.claim: Its name rearranges the letters of Joel Bean, the developer who laid out the town in the 1920s.
evidence.quote: The name El Jobean is an anagram of the letters of "Joel Bean", the name of the property developer who laid out the town site in the 1920s.

evidence.claim: A post office operated here from 1924 until 1964.
evidence.quote: A post office called El Jobean was established in 1924, and remained in operation until 1964.

evidence.claim: In 1928, a wooden bridge beside the railway brought the road across the Myakka to El Jobean.
evidence.quote: In 1928, the road was extended from McCall northeast over the Myakka River with a wooden bridge built next to the Charlotte Harbor and Northern Railway

evidence.claim: The wooden crossing was replaced by a concrete bridge in 1959; a second bridge followed in 2001.
evidence.quote: In 1959, the original wooden bridge over the Myakka River near El Jobean was replaced with a two-lane concrete bridge. A second two-lane bridge was built in 2001 when the road was widened to four lanes.

evidence.claim: The Myakka crossing began as a wooden bridge beside the railway in 1928, extending the road northeast from McCall to the developing town of El Jobean.
evidence.quote: In 1928, the road was extended from McCall northeast over the Myakka River with a wooden bridge built next to the Charlotte Harbor and Northern Railway

evidence.claim: Englewood Beach occupies the Charlotte County portion; farther along the peninsula, Manasota Beach lies in Sarasota County.
evidence.quote: The community of Englewood Beach occupies the Charlotte County portion of the key, while the Sarasota County part of the peninsula contains the community of Manasota Beach.

evidence.claim: The two concrete bridges divide traffic by direction: the 2001 span carries westbound vehicles, while eastbound traffic uses the 1959 bridge.
evidence.quote: The 2001 bridge carries westbound traffic and the 1959 bridge carries eastbound traffic.
